name: Vauchamps

art.title: Prussian infantry at Étoges, during Vauchamps

summary: Blücher, coming on with Kleist's and Kapzevich's corps against Marmont, met Napoleon instead; Grouchy's cavalry rode round the retreating allied squares, which fought their way back through the French horsemen to Étoges with heavy loss.

sources.label: French and Allied Forces, Battle of Vauchamps, 14 February 1814 (Nafziger Collection 814BAC)
Six Days' Campaign order of battle (Wikipedia)

forces.name: Ricard's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's division, which led the counter-attack on Zieten's brigade in Vauchamps as Blücher's advance ran into the Emperor's army, and followed it back along the road.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
Nafziger notes that Ricard's and Lagrange's divisions together had only about three thousand men by now.
Its fourteen battalions were what was left of whole regiments after Leipzig, 2,917 men in all, a couple of hundred each. They are shown at full size; the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.

Nafziger gives the division without its brigades. Its battalions are split between Fournier and Boudin as at La Rothière: the light battalions and the older line regiments with Fournier, the regiments raised in 1813 with Boudin.

Fournier's nine regiments and Boudin's five, where the list's brigade takes three, and five light battalions, where it allows one light regiment in the division, show as historical departures. Nafziger gives the division no guns.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lagrange's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's other division, which followed the allied retreat along the high road through the afternoon and took Étoges after dark.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
Nafziger notes that Ricard's and Lagrange's divisions together had only about three thousand men by now.
Its marine regiments were sailors and naval gunners of the fleet's artillery, brought inland in 1813; they fought well, and are shown as Line, the list's Veteran upgrade would suit them.

Nafziger gives the division as one brigade; its regiments are brigaded here as at La Rothière, after Nafziger's history as Wikipedia's order of battle has it. Battalion numbers he leaves out, and the division's artillery, are from his returns of 25 January and La Rothière.
Nafziger gives the 37th Line, but it is the 37th Léger, which served in the division at Leipzig; the 37th Line was in Duhesme's division of Victor's corps.
The division had 4,868 men in twenty-one battalions; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.

Marmont's artillery: three companies of the 3rd Foot Artillery from Nafziger's Vauchamps return, one with the division and two in the corps artillery, as the list takes them. Clavel's four regiments, where the list's brigade takes three, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

missing.name: Eight more foot companies and three horse companies
missing.reason: The rest of Marmont's corps artillery on Nafziger's return, the companies of the 2nd, 4th and 5th Foot and of three horse regiments, a few dozen gunners each.

forces.name: Leval's Division
forces.summary: Veterans brought from Soult's army in the Pyrenees that winter, just arrived and lent to Marmont, which moved out to come round the allied flank as Grouchy's cavalry did.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
The division had about 4,500 men in eight battalions, among the best in the army.
Nafziger gives the division two foot batteries and a horse battery; the second foot battery is in the reserve artillery here, as the list takes it.
Two light regiments, where the list allows one in the division, show as a historical departure. How far the division came into action isn't clear from Wikipedia's account.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

missing.name: Horse Battery
missing.reason: With no cavalry in the division to allow it.

forces.name: Saint-Germain's Cavalry
forces.summary: Grouchy's leading horse, which rode round Zieten's flank, cut off his brigade's retreat, and then charged again and again at the Prussian and Russian squares as they fell back along the road to Étoges.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
Nafziger gives the I and II Cavalry Corps together about 3,600 men.

Berckheim's 2nd Light Cavalry Division is Dommanget's and Jamin's brigades, and Saint-Germain's own 2nd Heavy Division Blancard's and Sopransy's. They were the regiments of Sébastiani's corps of 1813, a hundred or so men each by now; each is shown as one unit at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
The chevau-légers lanciers are the list's Lancers. Its two horse batteries are one in its divisional artillery and one in its reserve, as the list takes them.
Light brigades of six regiments and a heavy brigade of four, where the list's take four and three, and two heavy brigades, where it takes one, show as historical departures.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Bordesoulle's Cavalry
forces.summary: Grouchy's heavy horse, which came up late and joined in the last charges on the allied squares; in the night Doumerc's cuirassiers surprised Udom's Russians at Étoges.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
Nafziger gives the I and II Cavalry Corps together about 3,600 men.
Merlin's 1st Light Cavalry Division is Wathier's and Guyon's brigades; Bordesoulle's own 2nd Heavy Cavalry Division, about twelve hundred men, Thiry's and Laville's.

Each brigade was made up of squadrons from the depots of many regiments: Nafziger names their parent regiments but not their strengths. They are grouped here as one unit for each kind of horse in a brigade, or two where a brigade had many, as they were formed into provisional regiments.
Two heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, and cuirassiers and dragoons in one brigade show as historical departures.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lefebvre-Desnouettes's Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: With Laferrière's division under Nansouty, it pressed Zieten's left as Grouchy came round his right.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
Nafziger gives the two Guard cavalry divisions together about 3,500 men.
Its strengths are of 28 January: some 3,300 men, the grenadiers about nine hundred and the other regiments six to seven hundred each.
Nafziger gives the division without brigades; its regiments are brigaded here as the list takes them, the Gendarmes d'Élite as the small unit the chasseurs' brigade may have with it.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Laferrière's Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: With Lefebvre-Desnouettes's division under Nansouty, it pressed Zieten's left as Grouchy came round his right.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
Nafziger gives the two Guard cavalry divisions together about 3,500 men.

Lion's brigade was the chasseurs, about five hundred, and the Empress Dragoons, about seven hundred; Letort's the grenadiers, about eight hundred and fifty. The dragoons are with Letort's grenadiers here, as the list's heavy brigade takes them.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Friant's Old Guard
forces.summary: The Old Guard, marched up behind the cavalry from Château-Thierry and held in reserve; only one of its battalions came into action.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
Nafziger notes that the Guard infantry, his order of battle's other three divisions with it, wasn't seriously engaged.
The division had 4,796 men in eight battalions. The 1st Chasseurs and Grenadiers à Pied are the list's Old Guard, and the 2nd, raised in 1811, its Middle Guard.
Nafziger gives Michel as the commander of the chasseurs' brigade as well as of the 2nd Old Guard Division; the brigade is shown here without him.
Nafziger gives the Guard artillery together, seven foot and four horse batteries, not by division; the batteries here are those the list's brigades take.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Kleist's Corps
forces.summary: Blücher's leading corps, marching west on Montmirail to fall on Marmont, which met Napoleon's whole army instead. Zieten's brigade, ahead at Vauchamps, was broken and lost two thousand prisoners; the rest of the corps fell back along the high road to Étoges in squares, with Grouchy's horsemen riding round and through them, and Kleist and Prince August were nearly taken.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1813: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the 1813 brigade, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.
Nafziger gives the corps 13,500 men. The 7th Reserve Infantry's third battalion was taken whole in the retreat.

Each brigade's cavalry regiment, Landwehr or hussars, is attached to it as the list's small regiment. The list has no cuirassiers: the Silesian, East Prussian and Brandenburg Cuirassiers are its Dragoons, its only heavy cavalry.
Braun's reserve artillery is the list's: the 12-pdr batteries its Heavy Artillery, and the howitzer battery its Foot Artillery.

Nafziger numbers the 2nd West Prussian's battalions 1 to 3, without a fusilier battalion; all three are Musketeers here. Pirch's two regiments of three musketeer battalions, where the list's take two, brigades without Landwehr infantry, and more reserve artillery or cavalry brigades than the list allows for the corps, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Kaptsevich's Corps
forces.formation: X Infantry Corps, Army of Silesia
forces.summary: Langeron's corps marching with Kleist's, about 6,500 men, which fell back beside the Prussians in squares along the high road. Urusov's division, left at Étoges as a rearguard, was surprised there after dark and taken with eight guns.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Vauchamps, from the French archives and Clerc's history of Soult's campaign; its strengths are of 1 February.

Urusov's 8th Division (the first two brigades) and Turchaninov's 22nd (the last two). Its regiments had one or two battalions each, a few hundred men; each is shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.
Its three batteries, a position and two light, are with the brigades, as the list takes them.
Three infantry regiments in a brigade, where the list takes two, and two Jäger brigades, where it allows one, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 4 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

toCome.name: Udom's Division
toCome.summary: The fifteen hundred who had got away from Champaubert, made up into three or four combined battalions with a single battery, and surprised at Étoges after dark by Doumerc's cuirassiers; Nafziger notes their organisation isn't known.
